minimal_patch.value: Taken together, reported assistant use and demand for action rules indicate that retailer assistant experiences should pair convenience with user control.
Consumers rated several promotion formats similarly for purchase-decision effectiveness, so the survey alone offers limited basis for choosing one format over another.
The signals point to selective spending, not an across-the-board return to impulse buying: retailers should preserve value cues while making smaller purchase options easy.
The reported willingness to pay extra makes delivery speed a possible source of value differentiation for quick-commerce offers to this cohort.
71% of consumers say they would switch brands if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.
74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere.
